findings.reason: pinning the discarded record's filename to sort first, as §25's done-when already does for its incomplete record, is what makes the new case fail at base; without it the one case that isolates the discard rule is vacuous and the node can promote a selection it never proved.
findings.text: §27's second case puts a parsed record from a discarded run beside a parsed record from a promoted run, but states no order for the two files; `_select_stored_record` returns `path, record` for the first complete head match it meets while iterating the caller's sorted glob (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:494-504`), and with both records parsed the landed complete-preference distinguishes nothing, so the reader's answer is whichever filename sorts first. If the fixture names the promoted record first the second case passes on the unfixed selection and demonstrates nothing, and the negative control as written ("today's selection resolves the first case to the unparsed record") covers only the first case

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `promotion.discard_record_path` resolves at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:1941`, the dispose refusal quoted in the Why resolves at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1077`, `review.stored_record` is re-exported by `reckon/crew/review.py:3911` from `reckon/crew/review_records.py:564`, and the candidate's `review_run_id` the mechanism keys on is the field the store already requires a record to name.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §27's newly added second case does not pin the order in which the committed reader meets its two candidate files, so the case can pass on the unfixed selection.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate and negative control are logged "under the run directory", the durable path the plan's siblings use, and the new test lives under `tests/`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §27 introduces no symbol, filename or comment carrying a plan label, ticket number or version tag, and its new test is named for the behaviour it proves.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the Why's root cause matches the cited evidence: `_select_stored_record` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:450`) prefers a complete record at a named head but otherwise returns the first head match in the order the caller's sorted glob supplies, and a figure record reading `unparsed` (or parsed without the six dimensions and total `_review_is_complete` requires, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:1317`) never enters the complete branch, so the discarded record can win; the mechanism names a real predicate on a reachable read path, and `stored_record` — the caller `crew dispose` uses at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1067` — reaches that function for the figure rubric through `_review_rubric_matches` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:484`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §27 delivers one change, the discard-aware preference in the stored-record selection; its three cases and write paths all serve that one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §27 carries `data-status="implementable"`, appears as `s27: implementable` in `plan-section-declarations`, and the open followup `f-erikacr-027` names §27 as its invocation, so the section is dispatched and depends on nothing undeclared.
